sources.citation: Estermann, Carlos & António Joaquim da Silva. 1971. Cinquenta contos bantos do sudoeste de Angola: texto bilingue com introdução e comentários. Luanda: IICA. (2025 digital re-edition by José D. M. Muhona)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bilingual Nyaneka-Portuguese folktales with an ethnographic/performance introduction; remarks on 'tonalidades e inflexões de voz' refer to storytelling delivery, not phonology. Silent on stress/tone.

sources.citation: Homburger, L[ilias]. 1925. Le groupe sud-ouest des langues bantoues. Mission Rohan-Chabot, Angola et Rhodesia (1912-1914), Tome III, fasc. 1: Linguistique. Paris: Imprimerie Nationale / Paul Geuthner. 209 views (~190 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative phonetics (ch. III, pp. 85-104) and morphology of 7 SW-Bantu varieties incl. Nyaneka (data from the Huíla mission grammars, no Nyaneka informant). Only mention of accent is a general remark on p. 85 (view 105): consonant correspondences 'n'étant pas généralement influencées par l'accent (bien qu'il y ait des faits propres à la finale)'. Nyaneka-specific remarks (pp. 97-98) concern aspiration of N+voiceless and loss of nasals before final i. No word-stress rule, no tone marking, no accent marks in the transcription key (pp. v-viii).

sources.note: Google/Stanford scan on archive.org (diccionarioport00fathgoog). Dictionary body only; no preface or pronunciation note; no accent marks on Nyaneka forms. Silent on stress.
